name: Amon
overview: Amon was a male king of Judah and the son of Manasseh, known for doing evil in the sight of the Lord. His reign followed that of his father, and he continued in wickedness without repentance. Scripture highlights his brief and ungodly rule as a significant part of Judah's history.
namesAndTitles: The name Amon means "trustworthy," though this meaning contrasts with his actions as recorded in Scripture. He is also referred to by the title King Amon, emphasizing his royal status in Judah. Neither the name nor the title is described as being given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Amon was the son of Manasseh and Meshullemeth, and he was the father of Josiah. These relationships indicate a royal lineage in the kingdom of Judah, with Josiah succeeding Amon as king after his assassination.
scriptureSignificance: Amon's significance lies in his continuation of the evil practices of his father Manasseh, yet unlike Manasseh, he did not repent. His idolatry and sinful reign lasted only two years before he was assassinated by his own servants. Despite Amon's wickedness, God raised up his son Josiah, who would become a righteous leader and reverse Amon's corrupt policies, demonstrating God's sovereignty and grace.
